findings.note: The draft never says who should note this. The actor behind the recommendation is left unnamed.
"Realization" names the act of realizing, while the verb is the empty "had come to".

findings.quote: The decision to sell was made
findings.note: "Decision" carries the action while the verb is "was made"; the clause is also passive, so the actor who decided is absent. The action is buried in the noun.
"Evaluation" names the action while the verb "carried out" supplies only grammatical support. The act of evaluating is buried in the noun.

findings.quote: After eleven years of sitting in morning traffic behind a school bus,
findings.note: Thirteen words precede the main subject "I".
Doubled pair 'plain and simple' says one thing twice.
"picturesque" appears twice within two sentences, first in "a picturesque row of Victorian houses on Linden Street."

findings.quote: I reached the bottom of the hill by seven. I arrived at my desk with wet socks and a temper.
findings.note: Three consecutive sentences ("I left the house at six-forty. I reached the bottom of the hill by seven. I arrived at my desk...") all use the same first-person past-tense template, adding no structure.

findings.quote: an anchor that kept me moored to my own small concerns
findings.note: Mixed figure: the sentence first makes the car a cocoon and then an anchor, and a cocoon cannot also moor anything. The two images pull in incompatible directions within a single clause.
Stock simile that supplies no mechanism or picture; the following sentences do the actual work of describing what became visible.
Stock image standing in for an enclosure the draft never shows. The reader is given the label rather than the thing.

findings.quote: My bike was stolen in June.
findings.note: The previous sentence is about crossing the Fenwick Road bridge on foot. The opening introduces a bike, which nothing earlier in the paragraph prepared.

findings.quote: The combination was forgotten twice in the first week.
findings.note: The link to the lock appears only at the end of the previous sentence, after the new bike and new lock are the stated topic. The subject of this sentence is a combination that has not been mentioned.
The opening introduces "The walk" while the previous sentence was about forgetting other ways to cover the distance. The reference to the walk arrives only as a new element at the start.
The previous sentence was about the mechanic's transmission quote; the insurance renewal is a new element, though tied to the same week.

findings.quote: A monthly bus pass costs sixty.
findings.note: The previous sentence was about the car's annual costs; the bus pass is new and the link is only the implicit cost comparison.

The previous sentence ends on the car as a cocoon and anchor to the writer's own concerns. The new opening, "On foot the city", only becomes linked once the contrast is worked out at the end of the sentence.

findings.quote: Municipal snow contracts in our city
findings.note: The sentence opens on municipal snow contracts, an element nothing in the paragraph has introduced. The previous sentences were about the narrator's departure times and arrival at the desk.
The sentence opens on Fenwick Road sidewalks, new to the paragraph. The link to the previous sentence is only at its end, where the bus routes are mentioned.
The opening introduces the new element "Everyone's situation". The previous sentence was about the writer not telling others how to live, and mentioned no one else's situation.

findings.quote: Many people live too far from work
findings.note: "Many people" opens on a new element not carried by the previous sentence about one person's situation. The prior sentence supplied no group of people.

findings.quote: It should be noted that I am not trying to tell anyone else how to live. Everyone's situation is different, and what works for one person will not necessarily work for another. Many people live too far from work, or have children to drop off, or have jobs that require a car, and I do not want to suggest that any of them are doing anything wrong.
findings.note: Stacked qualification and restatement: the disclaimer is stated three times in successive sentences, and the final sentence repeats the limit already given in the first.

findings.quote: I can only describe what happened to me, in my own circumstances, which may or may not resemble yours.
findings.note: Stacked qualification: the scope limit is hedged twice in one clause, adding nothing to the disclaimer that precedes it.

'that February' and the hill have no antecedent where they stand; the winter timeframe and the route (Carver Hill) are supplied only by the later paragraph opening 'The first winter was very hard'. Until then the reader cannot place this scene relative to the April sale in 'The decision to sell was made in April'.
The draft never says who should note this. The surrounding sentences give no actor for the noting.
The draft never says who raised the concerns, though they are offered as evidence of a year-long problem.

findings.quote: It was decided in 2023 that all changes would go through this process
findings.note: The draft never says who made this decision. The surrounding sentences name the board only as the body that meets and posts decisions, not as the decider here, so the reader cannot tell whether the board, management, or someone else imposed the process.
The noun "review" buries the action, and the verb "conduct" does little work.
"determination" buries the verb "determine" behind the empty verb "makes".
Three consecutive sentences open with the same two words, "The board".

findings.quote: Given the results of the pilot and what both teams told us in the May retrospective,
findings.note: The main subject, "I", arrives after a sixteen-word introductory clause.
"full and complete" is a doubled pair saying one thing twice. The redundant second term adds nothing to "full".

findings.quote: a toll booth on the highway to production
findings.note: A stock image standing in for an argument the paragraph never makes; the figure supplies no mechanism the literal claim about approval delays would not.
Stock image: the constraint it names is never spelled out, so the figure carries the objection on its own.

findings.quote: Oversight would remain in place for the changes where it matters most, and that point should not be lost.
findings.note: Restatement of the point already made in "the board would still review every high-risk change".
The previous sentence is about the checklist and the weekly schedule; the link to that material only arrives at the end of this sentence, with "the delays".

New element at the opening: the median wait for approval has not been introduced in this paragraph, which until now was about approvals recorded and admission controllers. The previous sentence was about controllers rejecting a deploy whose ticket lacks a link.
Names 'the pilot' and 'both teams' before the paragraph 'In March and April, the Payments and Search teams ran a pilot' tells the reader what that pilot was and which teams ran it.

findings.quote: In March and April, the Payments and Search teams ran a pilot.
findings.note: The pilot topic is split: the paragraph 'Under the pilot, both teams' gives its results, paragraphs on the board's current process intervene, and this paragraph then returns to the pilot.

findings.quote: At a quarter past four on the ninth of March,
findings.note: Twelve words precede the main subject "Ellen Morrow".
"She" followed by a verb opens four consecutive sentences, forming a run of four.

findings.quote: In the weeks after the water went down and the loss adjuster had come round to photograph each and every room,
findings.note: The subject Ellen is preceded by 21 words of introductory material.

findings.quote: Flood warnings for Quay Street were not issued
findings.note: The draft never says who failed to issue the warnings. Responsibility for the timing is the point of the sentence.
No promiser is named. The sentence treats a broken promise as a cost but leaves out who made it.
"Decision" buries the verb "decide" behind the empty verb "made"; the actor's action is carried by the noun.

The action of undertaking is buried in the noun "undertaking" behind the empty verb "has given". The clause stacks a second nominalization, "assessment" carried by "carry out", so no actor performs anything.
The verb "carry out" does the work while the action sits in the noun "assessment".
Doubled pair: "each and every" says the same thing twice in the phrase "each and every room".

"She" plus a verb opens three consecutive sentences ("She rang", "She carried", "She went back"), and the fourth opens the same way ("She left"). The repeated subject-first template runs across four sentences.
"sodden" appears twice, the first time in the earlier sentence about the smell of sodden flour.
"affected" repeats from the paragraph's first sentence ("The flood affected many people") in the second sentence's clause. Same root, two sentences apart.
The sentence opens on Tom, who has not appeared in this paragraph; the only link to the previous sentence is the term sodden, which arrives after the subject.

The sentence opens on a new element, a wave of support, which the previous sentence about the bakery as the beating heart and a heart stopping does not prepare. The link to the prior sentence exists only through the loose metaphor at its end.

findings.quote: Since the election, the council has given an undertaking
findings.note: The sentence opens on the council, which the previous sentence, about the flood wall, has not introduced. The council is the new element at the opening.
The previous sentence is about Tom driving for flour. This sentence opens on a new element, gluten development, with no term linking it to the flour run.
The previous sentence ends on the hall via the trestle table, but the new element, the hall kitchen, is placed at the opening as the subject.

The sentence opens on Ellen, who was last named two sentences earlier and is not mentioned in the sentence immediately before it. The sentence before is about the reopening and the new tiles and raised ovens.

findings.quote: For the street, the flood was a wake-up call.
findings.note: The sentence opens on the street and the flood, which appear nowhere in the sentence before it; the link is carried only by the closing phrase. The sentence before is about Ellen and her Christmas orders.

findings.quote: harder to put a price on
findings.note: Stock image standing in for whatever the losses actually were. The draft never says what those things are, so the figure carries the whole claim.
Stock image standing in for an argument the draft does not make; nothing in the paragraph establishes what the street was being roused to do.
Second image extending the wake-up call in a way that cannot hold: a call is not answered by relocating flour, and the referent of it is left unresolved.

findings.quote: The bakery is the beating heart of Quay Street
findings.note: Stock image. The figure asserts centrality and stoppage without giving any mechanism or comparison the literal claim would not already carry.

findings.quote: lit a fire under the council
findings.note: Stock image, and the second image in the paragraph after the heart figure. It stands in for an argument about what the support actually caused the council to do.

findings.quote: The flood affected many people on Quay Street in many different ways
findings.note: Repeats the point already made in the paragraph beginning "It was obviously a shock to the whole street", which states that the flood struck the whole street and not only the bakery; this paragraph restates that same street-wide impact without a further point.
"There was" carries the noun "expectation," burying the verb "expect."
"Made" carries the noun "observation," burying the verb "observe."

findings.quote: decided by the committee that a decision would be made
findings.note: The action noun "decision" is carried by the empty verb "made", and the clause's other action is also buried in the noun "decision" paired with "decided", leaving no actor. Two nominalizations crowd one clause.
"Determination" names the action while the verb "be made" does little work.
The word "resolution" repeats within two sentences; the first occurrence is in "a resolution would be arrived at", and the phrase "was arrived at" is likewise repeated.

findings.quote: It is a feeling that is familiar. It is a feeling that recurs.
findings.note: Two consecutive sentences are built on the same "It is a feeling that ..." template.

The previous sentence is about the proposal and the committee's decision; this sentence opens on the members, who are only introduced by this phrase itself. The link to the proposal arrives late, in the pronoun "it".

The subject "The chair" is a new element; the previous sentence was about the resolution. Nothing before the sentence prepares the chair, and the link arrives only late, in the words "time had expired".

findings.quote: It was decided by the committee
findings.note: Repeats the first paragraph, which begins 'It was decided by the committee'.
Repeats the earlier paragraph beginning 'There was an expectation'.

findings.quote: Some of us left the room
findings.note: Repeats the earlier paragraph beginning 'Some of us left the room'.
